builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
summary: FLAMIA replaces standard high-precision attention kernels (e.g., FlashAttention in FP16/BF16) with fused low-precision MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 attention kernels purpose-built for NVIDIA Blackwell, including causal-leakage safeguards and packed variable-length document support. It requires Blackwell-generation hardware (B200/B300), custom kernel integration, and careful numeric validation; the gain materializes only on long-context causal packed-document training workloads. Failure modes include numerical divergence in low-precision pretraining if scaling or forward/backward consistency is mishandled, no benefit on non-Blackwell hardware, and limited applicability to inference or short-context workloads.
rationale: The method delivers a modest, hardware-locked training speedup that is inaccessible on the reader's 24 GB GPU and irrelevant to API-based work, so it merits monitoring rather than adoption.
technique: MXFP8/NVFP4 attention kernels for Blackwell GPUs

claims.statement: FLAMIA replaces standard high-precision attention kernels (e.g., FlashAttention in FP16/BF16) with fused low-precision MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 attention kernels purpose-built for NVIDIA Blackwell, including causal-leakage safeguards and packed variable-length document support. It requires Blackwell-generation hardware (B200/B300), custom kernel integration, and careful numeric validation; the gain materializes only on long-context causal packed-document training workloads. Failure modes include numerical divergence in low-precision pretraining if scaling or forward/backward consistency is mishandled, no benefit on non-Blackwell hardware, and limited applicability to inference or short-context workloads.
MXFP8 path accelerates combined forward/backward attention, including quantization, by 1.10–1.40x on B200 and 1.06–1.42x on B300 versus the fastest baseline per workload.
